title: AgingBank: a manually curated knowledgebase and high-throughput analysis platform that provides experimentally supported multi-omics data relevant to aging in multiple species.
authors: Gao, Yue; Shang, Shipeng; Guo, Shuang; Wang, Xinyue; Zhou, Hanxiao; Sun, Yue; Gan, Jing; Zhang, Yakun; Li, Xia; Ning, Shangwei; Zhang, Yunpeng
one_liner_zh: 该文构建衰老多组学知识库与高通量分析平台，虽含转录因子等调控元件数据，但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题核心无关。
abstract: Discovering the biological basis of aging is one of the greatest remaining challenges for biomedical field. Work on the biology of aging has discovered a range of interventions and pathways that control aging rate. Thus, we developed AgingBank (http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/AgingBank) which was a manually curated comprehensive database and high-throughput analysis platform that provided experimentally supported multi-omics data relevant to aging in multiple species. AgingBank contained 3771 experimentally verified aging-related multi-omics entries from studies across more than 50 model organisms, including human, mice, worms, flies and yeast. The records included genome (single nucleotide polymorphism, copy number variation and somatic mutation), transcriptome [mRNA, long non-coding RNA (lncRNA), microRNA (miRNA) and circular RNA (circRNA)], epigenome (DNA methylation and histone modification), other modification and regulation elements (transcription factor, enhancer, promoter, gene silence, alternative splicing and RNA editing). In addition, AgingBank was also an online computational analysis platform containing five useful tools (Aging Landscape, Differential Expression Analyzer, Data Heat Mapper, Co-Expression Network and Functional Annotation Analyzer), nearly 112 high-throughput experiments of genes, miRNAs, lncRNAs, circRNAs and methylation sites related with aging. Cancer & Aging module was developed to explore the relationships between aging and cancer. Submit & Analysis module allows users upload and analyze their experiments data. AginBank is a valuable resource for elucidating aging-related biomarkers and relationships with other diseases.
abstract_zh: 揭示衰老的生物学基础是生物医学领域尚存的最大挑战之一。关于衰老生物学的研究已发现一系列能够调控衰老速率的干预措施和通路。为此，我们开发了AgingBank（http://bio-bigdata.hrbmu.edu.cn/AgingBank），这是一个人工整理的综合性数据库和高通量分析平台，提供跨多个物种与衰老相关的实验支持的多组学数据。AgingBank包含来自超过50种模式生物（包括人类、小鼠、线虫、果蝇和酵母）研究的3771条经实验验证的衰老相关多组学条目。记录涵盖基因组（单核苷酸多态性、拷贝数变异和体细胞突变）、转录组 [mRNA、长链非编码RNA (lncRNA)、微小RNA (miRNA) 和环状RNA (circRNA)]、表观基因组（DNA甲基化和组蛋白修饰）、其他修饰与调控元件（转录因子、增强子、启动子、基因沉默、可变剪接和RNA编辑）。此外，AgingBank还是一个在线计算分析平台，包含五个实用工具（衰老景观、差异表达分析器、数据热图绘制器、共表达网络和功能注释分析器），以及近112项与衰老相关的基因、miRNA、lncRNA、circRNA和甲基化位点的高通量实验。癌症与衰老模块旨在探索衰老与癌症之间的关系。提交与分析模块允许用户上传并分析其实验数据。AgingBank是阐明衰老相关生物标志物及其与其他疾病关系的宝贵资源。
